      Hook output empty, exit 0, push allowed. The shell runs that exactly

      invocation looks like; blank only spans that are arguments to a
      non-git command, or detect the invocation before stripping and strip

      approach, a quoted `"push"` or `'push'` immediately after `git` in
      command position must still classify as an invocation.
  - id: F2
    severity: high
    title: Preprocessing fails open when mktemp or awk is unavailable
    detail: >
      The hook's own header promises a missing dependency degrades to a
      broader check, never a silent no-op. The new stripper breaks that.
      Probe A: TMPDIR=/nonexistent, command `git push origin main`, feature
      branch. mktemp fails, awk -f reads a missing file, CLASSIFY_TEXT is

      same command. Same result. Every failure in the stripping stage must
      fall back to classifying the raw COMMAND text (the pre-fix behavior,
      which over-denies but never under-denies), or deny outright. Check
      mktemp's exit status, check awk's exit status, and treat an empty

One more finding for round 2, from the background security review, F5 at MEDIUM. Add it to your round-2 scope alongside F1 through F4.

F5: the branch check resolves from the payload cwd, but the push can run elsewhere. `git -C /some/repo push origin feat` checks cwd's branch, not /some/repo's. `cd /some/repo && git push` is the same. And if cd fails or `git branch --show-current` returns empty (detached HEAD, not a repo), the hook falls through and allows. This gap predates the mission (the old hook had it too with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) but it is in your write set and the fix is small.

Required: (a) if the push invocation carries `-C <dir>`, resolve the branch in <dir> (relative paths resolve against cwd); (b) if the command has a `cd <dir>` in command position before the push, resolve the branch in <dir> (relative against cwd); (c) when the resolved directory cannot be entered, or the branch is empty, fail closed: deny with a reason line saying the branch could not be determined. Do NOT deny every command that contains `cd`; compound commands are normal here and the reviewer's suggestion to block them is rejected.

Keep the scope honest in the header comment: the destination-ref check is the primary gate and works from any directory; the branch check is the second line and covers a bare `git push` with no refspec.

Tests to add: `git -C <main-checkout> push` from the feature worktree cwd (deny); `git -C <feature-worktree> push origin feat/example` from the main checkout cwd (allow); `cd <main-checkout> && git push` from the worktree cwd (deny); payload cwd pointing at a non-repo directory with a plain push (deny, fail closed); detached HEAD in the temp repo with a plain push (deny).

#!/bin/bash
# PreToolUse Bash — block git push to main/master.
#
# Catches compound commands (cd … && git push, git commit && git push) by
# matching `git push` anywhere in the command, and inspects the pushed ref so
# `git push origin main` is blocked even from a feature branch. Enforcement
# does not depend on jq: the deny payload is emitted with printf, and the
# command and cwd are read via jq when present or a raw-payload sed scan
# otherwise, so a missing jq degrades to a broader check, never a silent
# no-op.
#
# Branch is resolved from the hook input's own cwd — the directory Claude
# Code ran the command from — not CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, which is always the
# main checkout regardless of which worktree a session is actually working
# in. Pushing a feature branch from its own worktree while the main checkout
# sits on main must be allowed; resolving branch from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
# denied that case outright. cwd is the fallback only when the input carries
# no cwd (older Claude Code payloads, or a caller that omits it).

INPUT=$(cat)

if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    COMMAND=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty')
    CWD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.cwd // empty')
else
    COMMAND=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"command"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\(\([^"\\]\|\\.\)*\)".*/\1/p')
    CWD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | sed -n 's/.*"cwd"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
fi

# Strip the interior of every single- and double-quoted substring, and every
# heredoc body, out of the command text before classifying it. A command's
# command-position regex (below) only cares whether `git push` appears as an
# actual invocation; the push phrase sitting inside a *multi-word* string
# literal or a heredoc body (a grep pattern, a commit message, prose written
# to a file) is data the command is handling, not an invocation, and must not
# be matched — so a multi-word quoted interior is blanked, but only when it
# itself contains the push phrase; a multi-word quoted literal that does not
# mention it is left untouched. A *single-word* quoted interior (no internal
# whitespace) is unquoted instead of blanked: `git "push"`, `git 'push'`, and
# a quoted destination ref (`git push origin "main"`) are all real shell
# tokens the invocation is actually built from, equivalent to their unquoted
# form — collapsing the quoting here is what lets the command-position check
# below recognize a quoted subcommand as the invocation it is, rather than
# treating the quoting itself as a reason to look away. Heredoc bodies are
# dropped by line, in full, since nothing inside one is a shell token at all.
# Double-quote interiors honor backslash-escaping like the shell does;
# single-quote interiors do not, matching shell quoting rules.
#
# The awk program is a quote-delimited heredoc (<<'AWK_EOF') fed to `awk -f`
# through process substitution rather than a temp file: its body contains
# literal single quotes (matching shell quote characters), and this whole
# script is itself invoked as a single-quoted string by hooks.json — a
# literal `awk '...'` here would close that outer quoting early, and a
# temp file written via mktemp makes the strip step depend on a writable
# TMPDIR for a security check that must never silently stand down when its
# environment is merely inconvenient. Process substitution needs nothing
# writable: it is piped straight from the shell's own heredoc buffer, so a
# missing or unwritable TMPDIR cannot take the stripper down with it.
strip_push_text() {
    awk -f <(cat <<'AWK_EOF'
function strip_quotes(line,    i, n, c, out, j, interior, quote, start, idx) {
    out = ""
    i = 1
    n = length(line)
    while (i <= n) {
        c = substr(line, i, 1)
        if (c == "'" || c == "\"") {
            quote = c
            start = i + 1
            if (quote == "\"") {
                j = start
                while (j <= n) {
                    if (substr(line, j, 1) == "\\" && j < n) {
                        j += 2
                        continue
                    }
                    if (substr(line, j, 1) == quote) break
                    j++
                }
            } else {
                idx = index(substr(line, start), quote)
                j = (idx == 0) ? n + 1 : start + idx - 1
            }
            if (j > n) {
                # Unterminated quote — not a closed token; pass the quote
                # character through literally and keep scanning.
                out = out c
                i++
                continue
            }
            interior = substr(line, start, j - start)
            if (interior ~ /[ \t]/) {
                out = out quote (interior ~ /push/ ? "" : interior) quote
            } else {
                # A single shell word with no internal whitespace: unquote
                # it, since quoting changes nothing about what word this is.
                out = out interior
            }
            i = j + 1
            continue
        }
        out = out c
        i++
    }
    return out
}

BEGIN { in_heredoc = 0; delim = ""; strip_tabs = 0 }

{
    line = $0
    if (in_heredoc) {
        test = line
        if (strip_tabs) sub(/^\t+/, "", test)
        if (test == delim) {
            in_heredoc = 0
            delim = ""
            strip_tabs = 0
        }
        next
    }

    if (match(line, /<<-?[[:space:]]*['"]?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*['"]?/)) {
        op = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        before = substr(line, 1, RSTART - 1)
        after = substr(line, RSTART + RLENGTH)
        strip_tabs = (op ~ /^<<-/)
        delimword = op
        sub(/^<<-?[[:space:]]*/, "", delimword)
        gsub(/['"]/, "", delimword)
        delim = delimword
        in_heredoc = 1
        print strip_quotes(before) op strip_quotes(after)
        next
    }

    print strip_quotes(line)
}
AWK_EOF
)
}

CLASSIFY_TEXT=$(printf '%s' "$COMMAND" | strip_push_text)
STRIP_STATUS=$?

# Fail safe, not fail open: if the stripper didn't run cleanly — awk missing
# from PATH, the process substitution's pipe broken, or any other failure —
# or if it silently swallowed a non-empty command into empty output, classify
# the raw, unstripped command instead of treating the failure as "nothing to
# see here." An unstripped command can only ever over-match (a quoted literal
# might wrongly look like an invocation) and fall through to the real-branch
# and destination-ref checks below, which independently decide allow/deny —
# never under-match and silently let a real push through. This is the
# opposite failure mode from a missing jq (which intentionally broadens, not
# narrows, what COMMAND already is); here the stripper is pure classification
# help and its absence must never narrow the set of commands this hook looks
# at.
if [[ "$STRIP_STATUS" -ne 0 || ( -z "$CLASSIFY_TEXT" && -n "$COMMAND" ) ]]; then
    CLASSIFY_TEXT="$COMMAND"
fi

# Only proceed when `git push` appears in command position — at the start or
# after a shell separator (&&, ||, ;, |, `(`), optionally behind leading env
# assignments (GIT_TRACE=1 git push …), with `git` and/or `push` optionally
# wrapped in a single matching quote char each (git "push", 'git' push …) —
# this catches compound, env-prefixed, and quoted-token invocations without
# false-matching the phrase inside a multi-word quoted literal or a heredoc
# body (both collapsed by the stripper above), which is not an invocation.
printf '%s' "$CLASSIFY_TEXT" | grep -qE '(^|[&|;(])[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+)*["'"'"']?git["'"'"']?[[:space:]]+["'"'"']?push["'"'"']?' || exit 0

deny() {
    printf '%s\n' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED: Cannot push to main/master. All changes go through PRs. Create a feature branch, push it, and open a PR."}}'
    exit 0
}

cd "${CWD:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}}" 2>/dev/null || true
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null)

if [[ "$BRANCH" == "main" || "$BRANCH" == "master" ]]; then
    deny
fi

# Scope the ref check to each `git push …` invocation's own arguments (up to
# the next shell separator), so main/master mentioned elsewhere in a compound
# command — echo text, an unrelated branch (`git push origin feat && echo
# see main`) — does not false-trigger. Within those args, deny main/master as a
# destination ref: bare (`origin main`), a refspec RHS (`HEAD:main`), or a full
# ref (`refs/heads/main`). A source-only refspec (`main:feature`, main followed
# by `:`) is not a push to the protected branch and is left alone. This reads
# the same classify text the command-position check used above, so a push
# invocation's genuine destination ref — including a quoted one, e.g. `git
# push origin "main"`, now unquoted to `main` by the stripper above — is
# still visible.
PUSH_ARGS=$(printf '%s' "$CLASSIFY_TEXT" | grep -oE '["'"'"']?git["'"'"']?[[:space:]]+["'"'"']?push["'"'"']?[^;&|]*')
if printf '%s' "$PUSH_ARGS" | grep -qE '([[:space:]:/])(main|master)([^[:alnum:]_/:-]|$)'; then
    deny
fi

exit 0
